description: The Cornetto Italian Butter Croissant is a beloved staple of Italian breakfast, a light and flaky pastry with a rich, buttery aroma. Its golden-brown exterior gives way to a soft, airy interior, often enjoyed plain or filled with cream or jam. This delightful treat perfectly complements a strong Italian espresso or cappuccino.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Gradually add the lukewarm milk, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Form into a ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Chill and Prepare Butter
instructions.text: Punch down the risen dough and gently shape it into a rectangle. Wrap it in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. While the dough chills, prepare the butter block. Place the cold butter between two sheets of parchment paper and roll it into a 15x15 cm square. Refrigerate the butter block.

instructions.title: First Turn
instructions.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll the chilled dough into a rectangle approximately 20x40 cm. Place the butter block on one half of the dough, leaving a 1 cm border. Fold the other half of the dough over the butter, sealing the edges. Roll the dough again into a 20x60 cm rectangle. Perform a single turn by folding one-third of the dough over the center, then the remaining third over that, like a business letter. Wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Second and Third Turns
instructions.text: Repeat the rolling and folding process (single turn) two more times, chilling the dough for 30 minutes between each turn. After the third turn, wrap the dough tightly and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight, to allow the gluten to relax and butter to firm.

instructions.title: Shape the Cornetti
instructions.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll the chilled dough into a large rectangle, about 3mm thick. Trim the edges to create clean lines. Cut the dough into long triangles with a base of about 8-10 cm. Starting from the wide base, gently roll each triangle towards the point, forming the classic cornetto shape. Curve the ends slightly to create the crescent.

instructions.title: Final Proof and Bake
instructions.text: Place the shaped cornetti on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until visibly puffy and almost doubled in size. Preheat oven to 190 degrees Celsius. Whisk the egg with 1 tablespoon of water for an egg wash. Gently brush the cornetti with the egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and flaky. Let cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

tips: Always use high-quality, cold butter for lamination; this is crucial for achieving distinct, flaky layers.
Do not overwork the dough during rolling and folding; use gentle, even pressure to prevent tearing and keep the butter intact.
Ensure adequate chilling time between turns to keep the butter firm and the dough relaxed, making it easier to work with and preventing butter from melting out.
